author.name: Carlo Collodi
author.biography: Born Carlo Lorenzini, he translated Perrault's fairy tales, and Pinocchio began as a magazine serial in 1881.

hook.text: What does it take for a puppet who keeps running away to find his way home?

paragraphs: An old woodcarver named Geppetto carves himself a puppet from a log that talks back. Before the puppet's feet are finished he is kicking; before the day is out he has run off and got his maker arrested. The puppet is Pinocchio, and he will spend the whole book running.

He means well every time. He promises to go to school, to bring the gold coins home, to be good tomorrow. Then a puppet show, a pair of smooth-talking swindlers or a friend with a better plan comes along, and he follows. The world he wanders through is hungry, unjust and full of people who want something from him, and Collodi shows it plainly: prison for the robbed, a noose in a tree, a farmer's dog collar, a buyer who wants a donkey only for its skin.

Against all this stand a few who never give up on him: Geppetto, who sells his only coat to buy him a schoolbook, and the Fairy with the blue hair, who scolds, forgives and waits. The book is funny, fast and often frightening, and its famous nose is only one of its jokes.
Read it as an adventure and as a question it keeps asking. What changes a person: punishment, kindness, hunger, or finally caring for someone else?

orientation.text: Thirty-six short chapters, each named by a summary of what happens in it. The narrator sometimes speaks to the reader directly. Animals talk, the dead come back, and nobody in the book finds that strange.
